claims.quote: Triple topical therapy is first-line treatment that is often effective

claims.text: only epidermal pigmentation responds (accentuated under a Wood light)
claims.quote: Other treatment depends on whether the pigmentation is epidermal or dermal; epidermal pigmentation becomes accentuated with a Wood light (365 nm) or can be diagnosed with biopsy. Only epidermal pigmentation responds to treatment.

claims.text: Hydroquinone blocks oxidation of tyrosine (DOPA) and inhibits melanocyte metabolism; tretinoin speeds keratinocyte turnover; the corticosteroid blocks melanin synthesis and secretion
claims.quote: Hydroquinone depigments the skin by blocking the enzymatic oxidation of tyrosine 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA) and inhibiting melanocyte metabolic processes. Hydroquinone should be tested behind one ear or on a small patch on the forearm for 1 week before use on the face because it may cause irritation or an allergic reaction. Tretinoin promotes keratinocyte turnover and can exfoliate skin that contains epidermal pigment. Corticosteroids help block synthesis and secretion of melanin.

claims.text: Test hydroquinone behind one ear or on the forearm for 1 week before facial use (irritation, allergy)
claims.quote: Hydroquinone should be tested behind one ear or on a small patch on the forearm for 1 week before use on the face because it may cause irritation or an allergic reaction.

claims.text: If triple therapy isn't available, hydroquinone alone can be used, but chronic continuous use can theoretically increase the risk of exogenous ochronosis (permanent hyperpigmentation); 2% suits maintenance
claims.quote: If triple topical therapy is not available, hydroquinone 2 to 4% alone can be used; however, chronic continuous use can theoretically increase the risk of exogenous ochronosis, which is a permanent form of hyperpigmentation. Hydroquinone 2% is useful as maintenance.

claims.text: Hydroquinone and tretinoin are not safe in pregnancy
claims.quote: Hydroquinone, tranexamic acid, trichloroacetic acid peels, and tretinoin are not safe to use during pregnancy.
